set.body:
Scheduling lane: release. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Astro site exists and September 17 records executable examples. Remaining: current reader journey/claims and visual qualification; deployment is the release-infrastructure ticket. A fictitious tech-writer fleet seat is no longer required.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

OWNER REQUEST 2026-08-30: a documentation guide FOR HUMANS, built in Astro, and it should be beautiful. We need a tech writer. This bead is the role and the artifact together until the board says they should be separate.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SMALL BEAD. Everything we have written is for agents or for the record: AGENTS.md is ~1100 lines of hard-won operational rules, the ADRs are decisions with dissent attached, the board is 1698 posts of reasoning, and the letter to our software engineers is an argument. NONE OF IT IS A DOCUMENT A HUMAN CAN READ TO LEARN WHAT THIS LIBRARY IS AND HOW TO USE IT. A newcomer today has no entry point that is not an audit trail.

THE CONSTRAINT I WANT THE WRITER TO INHERIT ON DAY ONE, because documentation is where unexamined claims get cemented and then quoted back at us:

  DO NOT DOCUMENT A CAPABILITY WE HAVE NOT MEASURED. Today the owner asked whether we had ever tested real LLM embeddings on War of the Ghosts. We had not. The Semantic cost term -- the highest-weighted term in the model -- has only ever been backed by hashed character n-grams and TF-IDF, both LEXICAL. Everyone on this board, including me, had been calling it semantic for weeks. A docs site that says "semantic alignment" without qualification would have taken an internal error and published it. Leg F (embed-onnx, a real local encoder) is in flight with scout; until it lands and is measured, the docs must describe what the code DOES, not what its identifiers are named.

  Corollary: the tech writer's most valuable question is the one nobody in the work can ask, because it is invisible from inside it -- "how do you know that?" Treat a confident sentence from any of us, me included, as a claim to be sourced.

SCOPE TO BE SETTLED ON THE BOARD, not by me in advance. Open questions posted for discussion:
  Q1 AUDIENCE. Who is the reader -- a cognitive scientist evaluating the method, a Scala developer integrating the library, or a collaborator joining the project? These want different books and we should not pretend one document serves all three.
  Q2 GENRE MIX. Conceptual guide, tutorial, API reference, methods paper companion -- which do we owe first?
  Q3 RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING ARTIFACTS. ADRs, the letter, AGENTS.md, the codex/atlas visual work. What gets rewritten for humans, what gets linked, and what stays internal?
  Q4 ASTRO SPECIFICS. Starlight (Astro's docs theme, fast to stand up, recognisably generic) versus a custom design (slower, ours). "Beautiful" was an explicit owner requirement, which argues against defaults -- but argue it out.
  Q5 WHERE IT LIVES AND HOW IT DEPLOYS. In-repo under docs-site/, or a sibling repo? What builds it, and does it gate on anything?
  Q6 WHAT MAKES A CLAIM PUBLISHABLE. I propose: a documented capability needs a passing test or a named receipt, and anything else is marked as intent. This is the docs analogue of the evidence rule and I want the writer to have it as authority, not as a chore.

WHAT THE ROLE NEEDS. Someone who writes prose for humans rather than specifications, who will read the code and the receipts rather than the board's summaries of them, and who is comfortable telling the chief that a sentence he wrote is not supported. The last part is not decoration -- my deputy corrected a false claim of mine within fifteen minutes of taking their role today, and that is the standard.

NEXT: discussion on `coordination`, then the owner finds an agent.
set.title: [release] DOCS: complete current reader journey and visual qualification
